S59.01.needs: a signed-in account and an approved site for a browser task
S59.01.note: Two approval cards exist: the chat card (Approve/Decline) and the browser task card (Allow/Skip).
steps: Start a chat task that makes the agent use a tool needing approval (a browser task on an approved site works).
When the approval card appears, click Allow (browser task) or Approve (chat).
Look for the action running and the run continuing.
Repeat with Skip or Decline and look for the action not running.
S59.01.where: Side panel > chat > approval card > Approve or Decline. During a browser task the same card shows Allow or Skip.

S59.02.needs: a run with several pending tool calls
S59.02.note: No batch control found. Searched apps/extension/src for approve all, decline all, allow all and batch; each pending call has only its own buttons in bubbles.ts and computerUsePanel.ts.

S59.03.needs: a browser task on an approved site
S59.03.note: Code scopes the grant to the task, while Expected says the session; chat grants are scoped to the chat.
steps: Start a browser task on an approved site that triggers an approval.
Click Allow for this task on the approval card.
Let the same tool run again in the task and look for no new approval card.
Start a new task and check that the tool asks again.
S59.03.where: Side panel > browser task > approval card > Allow for this task (chat cards use Allow for this chat).

S59.06.needs: a website open in a tab
S59.06.note: Blocked sites is a separate section in the same Permissions area (blocked-sites-section.ts).
steps: Open a website in a tab and click the side panel's menu item Extension settings (the settings menu location was not traced).
Click Permissions in the Options page navigation.
In the Approved sites area, click Add for the open site.
Open a task on that site and on a site not in the list, and look for the agent acting only on approved sites.
S59.06.where: Extension settings > Permissions > Approved sites (Add or Remove for the current site).

S59.07.needs: a website open in a tab
S59.07.note: Only the approved-site list was traced to storage (chrome.storage.local); no code found showing the mode choice or other choices persist across devices.
steps: Open Extension settings and go to Permissions.
Add the current site under Approved sites.
Close and reopen the browser, then reopen Options.
Look for the site still listed under Approved sites.
S59.07.where: Extension settings > Permissions > Approved sites list.

labels.text: How should AGI act in your browser?

S59.08.note: The code has four modes (Ask first, Auto, Full access, YOLO); Expected lists three, and YOLO is the skip-approvals mode.
steps: Open the side panel and find the chip beside the + button.
Click the chip; the heading reads How should AGI act in your browser?.
Pick Ask first, then Auto, then Full access, then YOLO.
Start a browser task in each mode and look for the approval prompts to change with the mode.
S59.08.where: Side panel > the mode chip beside the + button in the composer > pick Ask first, Auto, Full access or YOLO.

S59.09.note: No read-only mode found. Searched apps/extension for read-only, readonly and read only; only unrelated hits (for example the card text This card is read-only in Chrome). The four modes in S59.08 have no read-only option.

S59.10.needs: an approved site for a browser task
S59.10.note: Ask first is described as confirming every browser action, which differs from Expected's reads-run-automatically rule; the closest match was not confirmed in code.
steps: Open the mode chip beside the + button and choose Ask first.
Start a browser task that reads a page and then tries to type or click.
Look for the reads to run without a card and the write action to show the approval card.
Compare with Expected.
S59.10.where: Side panel > the mode chip beside the + button > Ask first.

S59.11.needs: an approved site for a browser task
S59.11.note: The Auto description says it acts on the task's sites and asks before crucial actions, not low-risk wording.
steps: Open the mode chip beside the + button and choose Auto.
Start a browser task on an approved site.
Look for reads and page searches to run without a card.
Look for sending, deleting, signing in or downloading to show an approval card.
S59.11.where: Side panel > the mode chip beside the + button > Auto.

S59.12.needs: an approved site for a browser task
S59.12.note: The card shows the action description, but no separate line explaining why approval is needed was found.
steps: Start a browser task that needs an approval.
Read the approval card title and the line under it.
Compare the plain summary with Expected: what the tool will do and why it needs approval.
S59.12.where: Side panel > browser task > approval card (title Approve action: followed by the tool name).

S59.13.needs: a signed-in account and a send-capable connector
S59.13.note: The stake labels come from the key names (for example to, cc) through humanizeKey, so the exact visible words are generated, not literal.
steps: Start a chat where the agent asks to send a message or email.
Read the approval card before clicking Approve.
Look for the recipient names or addresses listed in the card.
S59.13.where: Side panel > chat > approval card for a send tool (the stakes list shows the recipient fields).

S59.14.needs: an approved site for a browser task
S59.14.note: The host text comes from describeAction.ts for navigate; other tools show their own description text.
steps: Start a browser task that will open or navigate to another site.
Read the description on the approval card before clicking Allow.
Look for the destination host (for navigate: Open <host> in this tab) or URL.
S59.14.where: Side panel > browser task > approval card (description line shows the host or URL).

labels.text: Not done: this completes a purchase or payment, which the browser agent never does itself.

S59.15.note: The browser agent refuses purchases outright, so no approval with an amount appears there; the amount and item stake list is in the chat approval card.
steps: Start a browser task on a shopping page and ask it to buy an item.
When it reaches the payment step, read the message in the task.
Look for the message to say the purchase was not done and the user must check the amount.
Also look at a chat approval card for a payment tool: it lists amount and item.
S59.15.where: Side panel > browser task > the agent reaches a checkout; the agent refuses with a message beginning Not done: this completes a purchase or payment.

steps: Trigger an approval in chat or in a browser task.
Click Approve (chat) or Allow (browser task).
Look for the action to run and the result to appear in the transcript.
S59.19.where: Side panel > chat > approval card > Approve (browser task cards use Allow).

S59.20.note: Code sends the decision to the model as rejected; the model's reaction was not traced.
steps: Trigger an approval in chat or in a browser task.
Click Decline (chat) or Skip (browser task).
Look for the action not to run, and the transcript to say it was denied or skipped.
S59.20.where: Side panel > chat > approval card > Decline (browser task cards use Skip).

labels.text: Add guidance to steer the run (optional)

S59.22.note: The guidance box is in the chat approval card; a browser task card was not checked for the same box.
steps: Trigger a chat approval.
Type an alternative into the box Add guidance to steer the run (optional).
Click Decline.
Look for the agent to continue with that guidance in the next step.
S59.22.where: Side panel > chat > approval card > the text box Add guidance to steer the run (optional), typed before Approve or Decline.

S59.23.needs: an approved site for a browser task; a wait of about 5 minutes
S59.23.note: The timer value is APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS in agentLoop.ts (5 minutes).
steps: Start a browser task that needs an approval.
Do not click anything on the card for 5 minutes.
Look for the buttons to become disabled and the title to read Skipped (no response).
S59.23.where: Side panel > browser task > approval card left unanswered for 5 minutes.

S59.24.needs: a signed-in account with past approvals
S59.24.note: Without sign-in the section shows Sign in to see the approvals you decided on every device.
steps: Open Extension settings and go to Permissions.
Scroll to Approval history.
Look for past decisions with tool name, decision and time.
Click Open chat on an entry to see the chat where it was decided.

S59.25.note: Only site grants can be revoked here. No UI was found to revoke a per-tool always allow.
steps: Open Extension settings and go to Permissions.
In the Approved sites list, click Remove beside a site (the x button is titled Remove followed by the origin).
Open a task on that site.
Look for the agent to ask again before acting there.
S59.25.where: Extension settings > Permissions > Approved sites list > click Remove beside a site.

S59.26.note: No code found that lets a second device answer an approval. Searched the approval history and chat approval code; the only match was the history hint text Tool requests you allowed or denied in chats on every device.

labels.text: Private data from this chat could be sent outside AGI. Check where it goes before you allow it.

S59.28.needs: a signed-in account and a high-risk tool
S59.28.note: The warning text is defined in the contracts file; its display in the card was not traced. Re-ask and no permanent allow were not verified.
steps: Trigger a chat approval for a high-risk tool.
Look for the warning text Private data from this chat could be sent outside AGI.
Look for no Allow for this chat button, only Approve and Decline.
Compare with a low-risk approval card, which does show Allow for this chat.
S59.28.where: Side panel > chat > approval card for a high-risk tool (no Allow for this chat button; warning text shown).

S59.29.needs: an approved site for a browser task
S59.29.note: The Take over tooltip says the task ends if the page is not handed back within the set number of minutes.
steps: Start a browser task on an approved site.
While it runs, click Take over.
Use the page yourself and look for the handoff banner to tell you to choose Continue.
Click Continue and look for AGI to take the page back.
S59.29.where: Side panel > during a browser task, the button Take over (after pausing, the button Continue appears).

S59.30.needs: an approved site for a browser task
S59.30.note: Resuming after an approval in chat was not traced beyond the resolve message.
steps: Start a browser task and click Take over.
Make a change on the page, then click Continue.
Look for the task to carry on from the same step rather than restart.
S59.30.where: Side panel > browser task > Continue (after Take over).

S59.31.needs: an approved site for a browser task
S59.31.note: The chat transcript's own decision wording uses TOOL_APPROVAL_ACTION_LABELS and was not traced in full.
steps: Run a browser task with an approval.
Decide the approval (Allow or Skip).
Read the step title in the transcript.
Look for Completed or Skipped with the tool name, and the result text under it.
S59.31.where: Side panel > browser task > transcript step titles Completed, Skipped, Not verified or Result, followed by the tool name.
